page.layout: Two woodcut diagrams of spheres at the top (full width, no text); below them one column of running text, full width; a catchword-like word "nec" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: sistit & innititur plano Horizontis, & Æquator, qui medium inter polos locum exactè obtinet, cum Horizonte rectum constituit angulum sphæricum, à quo Recta cognominatur. Talem sphæræ mundi situm habent, qui sub Æquatore uersantur.

Obliqua seu decliuis seu inclinata sphæra, ἐγκεκλιμένη σφαῖρα, est, in qua alter polorũ mundi ab Horizonte eleuatus eminet, alter infra Horizontem decumbit & subsidit, & æquator cum Horizonte angulos efficit ac conformat obliquos, obtusum eum, qui polum eleuatum respicit, acutum, qui uergit ad oppositum. Talem habent sphæram, qui ultra citraq; æquatorem degunt. Sed non eadem est sphæræ obliquæ habitudo ubiq;, nec

page.notes: Diagram labels: left sphere "AEQVA(TOR)", "ORIZON", "RECTA"; right sphere "AEQVI(NOCTIALIS)", "AXIS", "ORIZON", "OBLIQ(VA)". Greek word "ἐγκεκλιμένη" is partly illegible in the scan and reconstructed from context. Word "nec" at the bottom right is the catchword. Running head and page number not printed.
